statusDefinitions.enforced: Every named control for the narrowly described current surface has implementation and automated verification evidence.
statusDefinitions.partial: Useful controls exist, but one or more documented attack paths or lifecycle requirements remain unqualified.
statusDefinitions.planned: The surface is not supported and must remain disabled until its acceptance criteria are implemented and verified.
statusDefinitions.release-blocked: The current controls are insufficient for production qualification of the named surface; the recorded gate must remain pending.

risks.title: Malformed or oversized project documents
risks.actor: A user or collaborator supplies a corrupt or adversarial project document.

currentControls.summary: Core project migration validates supported schemas and opens newer schemas read-only without overwriting them.
AUP4 conversion sanitizes imported records and is exercised with corrupt and compatibility fixtures.

residualRisks.exposure: Format-specific parsers do not yet share a single byte, node, depth, or elapsed-time budget.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Apply documented per-format and aggregate budgets before persistence.
acceptanceCriteria: Boundary tests reject oversized and deeply nested project fixtures before any project or source write.

residualRisks.exposure: The maintained malformed-project corpus does not yet cover every supported project family.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Maintain regression and fuzz fixtures for each supported project parser.
acceptanceCriteria: CI runs parser corpus tests with storage publication assertions for each family.

risks.title: Malformed media and metadata consume excessive resources or escape validation
risks.actor: An imported audio, video, metadata, or codec-argument payload is corrupt or adversarial.

currentControls.summary: WAV chunk iteration, metadata sizes, channel counts, and compressed ADM XML expansion have explicit bounds.
Custom FFmpeg exports use allowlisted protocols and reject extra inputs, reports, and unbounded arguments.

residualRisks.exposure: Compressed audio and video decoders lack a broad maintained malformed-input corpus and resource-budget gate.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Add codec-family corpus tests and explicit decode memory, output, and elapsed-time budgets.
acceptanceCriteria: CI exercises truncated, oversized, recursive, and decompression-amplification fixtures without publishing partial output.

residualRisks.exposure: Future native decoding is not yet isolated from the UI process or covered by crash quarantine.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Run native decoders in a supervised helper with bounded IPC and documented OS sandbox policy.
acceptanceCriteria: Helper crash, timeout, oversized output, and malformed-message tests leave the editor process responsive.

risks.title: Portable project archive paths and descriptors reference unintended or altered content
risks.actor: A .scape archive contains unsafe names, duplicates, inconsistent descriptors, or altered payload bytes.

currentControls.summary: Import rejects absolute, backslash, traversal, and duplicate names, validates manifest descriptors, and verifies extracted size and SHA-256 before publishing the project.

Import and inspection share a strict metadata envelope that rejects encrypted and directory entries, duplicate source or entry ownership, reserved-entry reuse, descriptor aliases, missing entries, and unreferenced extra entries before project or source storage writes.

After project migration, import and inspection require equal source/descriptor counts, unique exact case-sensitive source IDs, and identical audio/video kinds before collision handling, transaction creation, or any storage call.

risks.title: Portable project archive expansion exhausts memory, storage, or execution time
risks.actor: A .scape archive uses large metadata, misleading sizes, compression amplification, or a malicious PCM header.

currentControls.summary: Import caps entry count, validates hashes after extraction, aborts a failing audio writer, deletes already staged sources, and saves the project last.
A strict TypeScript envelope validates the entry-count limit and safe integer compressed/uncompressed metadata for every file before reading manifest bytes.
Manifest JSON is capped at 32 MiB and project JSON at 256 MiB using both central-directory preflight and byte-counted streaming text sinks.
The envelope rejects central-directory declarations whose safe cumulative uncompressed size exceeds 64 GiB before reading any entry body.

One shared budget counts bytes actually emitted into the manifest, project, and every extracted asset sink, rejecting cumulative output above 64 GiB before the over-budget chunk is retained or published.

Audio extraction validates each four-byte frame header against the shared 65,536-frame and 64-channel geometry limits before checked byte-length calculation or allocation; parser-owned pending storage is capped at 16 MiB plus the header.

Before manifest extraction, every entry runs zip.js strict local-header validation and pairwise entry-range overlap detection without decompressing its body; tested method disagreements and nested entry ranges reject before storage work.

A bounded raw-layout preflight, under a shared non-raiseable 33 MiB central-directory cap, anchors exact classic/Zip64 end and central-directory records, validates every central/local header and data descriptor without reading payloads, and rejects gaps, overlap, or entry ranges crossing the central directory before zip.js construction. Export admission reserves the pinned writer's greater-than-4-GiB Zip64 offset branch so produced archives remain admissible.

Archive enumeration is hard-capped at 4,096 entries, bounding zip.js pairwise layout comparisons, and one archive-wide budget is capped at 65,536 canonical PCM chunks before another source-writer call or chunk allocation.
Every project or asset descriptor must exactly match its entry's declared uncompressed size before project JSON or asset extraction begins.
The manifest, project, and asset descriptors must own distinct expected entries, and all extra, alias, missing, directory, or reserved-name entries are rejected before storage work.
Any encrypted central-directory entry rejects the archive before manifest or project bytes are read.
Inspection and import call the same strict archive-envelope validator; an integration test proves both reject the same extra entry before storage writes.
Central-directory indexing requires ZIP STORE and equal compressed/uncompressed sizes before local-header preflight or body reads; canonical exports pin the same policy.

Original video entries emit at most 4 MiB per zip.js chunk, are charged and independently hashed before each awaited transactional storage write, and must match declared size and SHA-256 before publication. OPFS receives bounded writes; IndexedDB uses source-owned native Blob chunks; process-memory fallback rejects payloads above 64 MiB before extraction. Cancellation, metadata drift, and failed publication remove staging and preserve prior inventory.

Canonical save output is re-chunked to at most 4 MiB, constrained by the admitted archive maximum, and verified by independent byte counts before publication. File System Access and desktop project targets remain staged until an explicit commit; desktop additionally negotiates one-MiB acknowledged IPC writes and synced rename. The non-streaming browser-download fallback retains its non-raiseable 512 MiB final-Blob ceiling.

The tested .scape open/save path propagates one task AbortSignal through ZIP enumeration and extraction, source reads and writes, archive output, and file publication. Cancellation closes readers, returns source iterators, aborts unpublished destinations and audio writers, deletes provisional media, and restores the prior project plus its retained revisions.

risks.title: Current Electron renderer IPC reaches privileges outside the versioned bridge
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content attempts to invoke arbitrary Electron or Node.js capabilities.

currentControls.summary: The renderer has context isolation, no Node integration, a sandbox, and a frozen input-validating v1 bridge.
Main-process handlers require the expected webContents and root document URL while navigation, new windows, webviews, and unapproved permissions are denied.

risks.title: Current desktop static-resource requests escape the packaged application root
risks.actor: Renderer content crafts an encoded path, symlink path, method, or range request.

currentControls.summary: Static requests are decoded, canonicalized, constrained by realpath containment, limited to safe methods, and protected by the desktop CSP.

risks.title: Desktop read capabilities leak paths, outlive their owner, or allow unbounded working sets
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content reuses or accumulates capabilities, or triggers a large whole-file read.

currentControls.summary: User selection opens a regular file first, returns a high-entropy expiring token rather than a path, and serves bounded single ranges from the pinned handle.

residualRisks.exposure: Capabilities lack a renderer-owner binding, renderer-destroy cleanup, and an aggregate per-session count/byte policy.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Bind capabilities to the creating webContents and close them on release, expiry, navigation, destruction, and aggregate-budget eviction.
acceptanceCriteria: Lifecycle tests prove cleanup on renderer destruction and deterministic refusal at aggregate capability limits.

residualRisks.exposure: The renderer file service materializes selected files as whole Blobs and does not propagate cancellation to fetch.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Use AbortSignal-aware bounded streaming or explicit format-size admission before Blob materialization.
acceptanceCriteria: Large-file and abort tests demonstrate bounded memory and immediate handle release.

risks.title: Desktop saves overwrite unintended paths, leave partial files, or exhaust disk
risks.actor: Compromised renderer content reuses a target or sends inconsistent, oversized, or interrupted chunks.

currentControls.summary: A user-selected target becomes a short-lived single-use token; sequential one-MiB chunks are checked against an exact length and committed by synced same-directory rename with abort cleanup.

Only project save capabilities may select bounded streaming mode. Main rejects writes above the archive-admitted maximum, waits for an active chunk acknowledgement before abort cleanup, and removes sessions on navigation, renderer loss, window close, or shutdown; explicit finish remains the sync-and-rename commit boundary.

residualRisks.exposure: Active sessions are cleaned on main-frame navigation, renderer loss, window close, and shutdown, but unconsumed target capabilities are not owner-bound and aggregate session/disk capacity is not preflighted.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Bind every target and session to its webContents owner, enforce aggregate product working-set limits, and preflight available storage.
acceptanceCriteria: Renderer-destruction, capacity, aggregate-session, and practical maximum-size tests fail without replacing the destination.

residualRisks.exposure: A bounded IPC chunk must finish or fail before abort closes staging; sync/rename is the non-cancellable commit boundary, and parent-directory durability is not qualified.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Define the cancellation acknowledgement and platform durability contract for active save operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Fault-injection tests cover cancellation during write, sync, and rename on every supported desktop platform.

risks.title: Current user-authored Nyquist source escapes its bounded WebAssembly worker envelope
risks.actor: A Nyquist program loops, requests excessive memory or output, or attempts file access.

currentControls.summary: Nyquist runs in a dedicated worker with validated protocol and source/input/output bounds, a 256-MiB WebAssembly memory ceiling, timeout and abort termination, and disabled C file-I/O stubs.

risks.title: Future third-party Web effect packages gain same-origin JavaScript authority
risks.actor: A future reviewed effect package is malicious, compromised, or has a confused-deputy import surface.

currentControls.summary: The maintained registry currently exposes only reviewed, source-pinned bundled Nyquist plug-ins; no generic package loader exists.

residualRisks.exposure: A reviewed Web effect package ABI, import allowlist, signature/hash policy, revocation model, and worker lifecycle are not implemented.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Instantiate pure WebAssembly packages in dedicated workers through a minimal allowlisted host ABI; do not import arbitrary third-party JavaScript into the application origin.
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed ABI, forbidden import, timeout, oversized output, hash mismatch, and revocation tests pass before a package loader is exposed.

risks.title: Future native media and render helpers compromise the UI process or remain alive after cancellation
risks.actor: Malformed input, a compromised helper binary, or a protocol peer sends invalid messages or refuses shutdown.

currentControls.summary: The current versioned preload bridge exposes no native helper, process-spawn, or plug-in-host channel.

residualRisks.exposure: No bounded helper protocol, process supervisor, sandbox policy, crash quarantine, or binary attestation exists.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Define a versioned bounded IPC protocol and supervised process lifecycle with least-privilege OS policy and verified binaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Crash, hang, malformed message, oversized payload, binary mismatch, and cancellation tests pass without exposing raw spawn authority to the renderer.

risks.title: Future native audio or video plug-ins execute with ambient user-account authority
risks.actor: A third-party VST3, CLAP, AU, LV2, or OFX binary is malicious, vulnerable, or incompatible.

currentControls.summary: The current renderer bridge and editor registry expose no native plug-in discovery, loading, or execution surface.

residualRisks.exposure: No plug-in discovery allowlist, quarantine, permissions, compatibility process, consent UX, or signing policy exists.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Treat native plug-ins as arbitrary code, isolate them in a supervised host, minimize filesystem and network authority, and disclose residual OS authority to the user.
acceptanceCriteria: Host compromise, crash recovery, denial, scanning, consent, revocation, and per-platform packaging tests pass before discovery is enabled.

risks.title: Cancelled or superseded jobs continue consuming resources or publish late results
risks.actor: A user cancels, switches projects, closes a renderer, or starts a replacement task while I/O is active.

currentControls.summary: Controller tasks receive AbortSignals and generation checks prevent stale results from replacing current UI state.

Native .scape open/save tasks pass their AbortSignal through archive, tested storage, and file publication boundaries; cancellation rolls staged assets and project revisions back before the task settles.

Within one project-store instance, clear and close stop writer admission, actively abort staged chunk or OPFS sinks, wait for terminal cleanup, and prevent a stalled OPFS write or shutdown race from publishing late state.

Project saves choose one target before asynchronous flush, stream through a plan-aware bounded destination, abort staging on project switch or failure, compare independent exact byte counts, and perform one explicit non-cancellable publication commit. Cancellation after a successful commit is reported as committed without stale success UI.

residualRisks.exposure: The tested native .scape open/save and direct-save publication paths now propagate and roll back cancellation, but inspection has no owned controller task and AUP4, whole-file desktop reads, broad storage operations, and remaining desktop transports do not share that qualified contract.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Propagate one signal through every long-job layer and acknowledge cancellation only after readers, writers, workers, and staged records are closed or rolled back.
acceptanceCriteria: Cancellation during read, parse, source write, project save, file write, and project switch leaves no late publication or orphaned session.

residualRisks.exposure: Active streamed-media coordination currently covers one project-store instance. Cleanup or clear initiated by another tab or store instance cannot yet abort or durably retain that writer's unpublished token or OPFS path.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Publish a durable cross-context staging lease or equivalent ownership record, validate it at every write/publication boundary, and invalidate it atomically during destructive maintenance.
acceptanceCriteria: Two-store IndexedDB and OPFS tests prove cleanup preserves a live writer, clear prevents its late publication, and expired/crashed staging is eventually reclaimed.

residualRisks.exposure: Project I/O progress has no consistently exposed user cancel action and close/navigation teardown contract.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Expose cancel for long project operations and bind teardown to navigation, renderer destruction, and application shutdown.
acceptanceCriteria: Browser and desktop workflow tests cancel an active import/export and verify prompt, recoverable return to the editor.

risks.title: Runtime binaries or release assets differ from reviewed source and policy
risks.actor: A compromised registry, build input, update source, or release process substitutes an executable artifact.

currentControls.summary: StaffPad, Nyquist, Parametric EQ, and WavPack record source and binary hashes and have fail-fast audit scripts.
Desktop packaging applies Electron fuses and checks packaged ASAR integrity before preview smoke tests.

residualRisks.exposure: External FFmpeg publication is not yet tied to a single digest, corresponding-source, notice, and security-policy gate.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Gate every runtime upload and desktop assembly on one reviewed manifest and fail closed before network publication.
acceptanceCriteria: Tampered, incomplete, or unreviewed runtime manifests prevent upload and desktop assembly in offline unit tests.

residualRisks.exposure: Desktop preview artifacts are unsigned and update signing, notarization, rollback, and key-rotation procedures are not production-qualified.
residualRisks.requiredControl: Qualify signed update publication, platform signing/notarization, rollback, and key compromise response.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-platform release drills verify signature rejection, rollback, provenance, and key rotation before stable auto-update is enabled.
